extracted.intended_audience: educators, education students, and educational policymakers/curriculum designers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts principles and evaluative criteria for educational practice from a philosophical treatment of education (Dewey): heredity vs environment, appropriate subject matter, nature of educative experience, social reconstruction, and the democratic ideal in schooling. Focuses on what makes experience educative and what social conditions education should promote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heredity as original endowment (heredity is a limit of education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heredity means the original endowment of an individual; education must take the being as he is. The fact of inheritance does not predetermine future use; rather it is a limit that determines what the educator can and cannot utilize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do a careful study of native aptitudes and deficiencies as a preliminary necessity, but avoid assuming inheritance fixes destiny. Example/anti-pattern: treating inheritance as predetermining future use wastes effort (advisor analogy). "Heredity is a limit of education."

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnish an environment adequate to existing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Once native activities exist, the crucial educational task is to provide an environment that will adequately function whatever activities are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration with language: if vocal/auditory equipment exists, whether a person learns a particular language depends on the social environment; if equipment is lacking, instruction is futile. Emphasize shaping surroundings to select and coordinate existing capacities rather than attempting to create absent ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper subject matter — use past products only as resources for present problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper subject matter of instruction is to keep the process of growth alive in the present; cultural products of the past are valuable only insofar as they enter into and inform present life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making the records and remains of the past the main material of education, which cuts the connection between present and past and makes culture an ornament or refuge. The past should be used to direct the present's movement; the present generates problems that give meaning to searching the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as reconstruction (reorganization) of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is the continuous reconstruction or reorganization of experience which (a) adds to the meaning of experience and (b) increases ability to direct the course of subsequent experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical definition: reconstruction increases perception of connections among activities and enhances capacity to intend consequences. The educative process identifies end and process together: experience completed reveals meaning of earlier portions. Both personal and social reconstruction count. Concise phrasing from text: "It is that reconstruction or reorganization of experience which adds to the meaning of experience, and which increases ability to direct the course of subsequent experience."

rubrics_metrics.name: Increment of meaning as criterion of educative experience
rubrics_metrics.description: An educative experience results in increased perception of connections and continuities among activities, i.e., an increment of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a child learns the link between sight, touch, heat after touching a flame; a scientist perceives connections through experimental acts. Instruction should lead learners to perceive such relations rather than leaving actions blind or disconnected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added power of subsequent direction/control as criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: An educative experience must increase a learner's ability to anticipate and direct future outcomes—i.e., to intend consequences and prepare in advance for beneficial results or avert harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes genuine education from mere routine or capricious action: education enables better anticipation and deliberate preparation; it transforms blind activity into intentional action with perceived bearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid capricious (aimless) activity in instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Capricious or aimless activity—where the actor "does not care what happens" and does not connect actions with consequences—does not produce educative experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: school tasks that are tricks or miracles to pupils because they do not see the connection between method and result lead to capricious habits. Such activity often arises from maladjustment with surroundings or external dictation that fails to elicit personal purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mere routine skill that lacks perception of bearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine, automatic action may increase specialized skill but does not lead to new perceptions of connections; it limits the meaning-horizon and can become disastrous when conditions change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While routine may improve a specific skill, it does not constitute genuine education unless it also broadens the learner's understanding of relations and applicability. Overemphasis on rote procedures is a persistent anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education integrates process and end (experience as continuous whole)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should identify process and end: learning is an active process over time whose later phases complete and give meaning to earlier ones; the whole continuous experience is educative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional design should create sequences of activity whose unfolding reveals prior meaning and establishes dispositions toward continued engagement; both earlier and later phases must be connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of experience can be social as well as personal
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational reconstruction operates at the social level: deliberate education can shape young people so that future society is improved rather than merely reproducing current habits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use education consciously to eliminate obvious social evils and to construct better social arrangements; recognize education's potential efficacy as a constructive agency for societal improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure for worth of a mode of social life (two-part criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: To evaluate the quality of a social group's educative effect ask: (1) How numerous and varied are the interests which are consciously shared? (2) How full and free is the interplay with other forms of association?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to examples: criminal band (few shared interests, isolated) vs family (many communicable interests, rich interconnections). The text gives the questions verbatim: "How numerous and varied are the interests which are consciously shared? How full and free is the interplay with other forms of association?" Use these as evaluative probes of social life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic ideal for education — mutual interpenetration and free interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: A democratic society is characterized by more numerous and varied shared interests and freer interaction between social groups; education in such a society must promote these traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications for education: democracies should emphasize deliberate, systematic education; ensure intellectual opportunities are accessible to all on equable terms; foster voluntary dispositions and interests rather than external authority; promote personal initiative and adaptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education must foster personal initiative and adaptability in mobile societies
rubrics_metrics.description: In societies marked by mobility and change, education should develop individuals' capacity for initiative and adaptability so they can perceive significance and connections amid rapid change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to do so will lead to confusion where a few appropriate results of others' blind activities. Education must prepare people to respond intelligently to changing circumstances and to participate in distribution of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize uniqueness and indefinite plurality of individual capacities (critique of Plato's classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should acknowledge the uniqueness of each individual and the indefinitely numerous and variable original capacities, rather than reducing people to a few fixed classes of faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Plato's insight to discover aptitudes and train for social use is valuable, avoid his lumping of individuals into a few classes; education must cultivate diverse capacities and resist static stratification that limits growth.
